Fixes bug B-dup-check-sibling-template-tasks: Filing ATF-junie-descriptor, ATF-continue-descriptor and ATF-zed-descriptor with the same title pattern as ATF-kiro-descriptor was refused as a possible duplicate (score 0.68-0.79) although each is a different agent; every add needed --new, and the refusal printed the answer command four times identically. Sibling per-agent tasks differ only by the agent name, which the similarity score underweights. Found on DRV-decide.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-dup-check-sibling-template-tasks --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-dup-check-sibling-template-tasks --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-dup-check-sibling-template-tasks: duplicate check refuses sibling tasks filed from one template

data.reason: False finding at the similarity engine. (1) The distinguishing per-agent token is already maximal-weight, not underweighted: against the real corpus IDF, 'junie'/'kiro'/'zed' have df=1 (idf 6.77, the ceiling), yet siblings still score 0.72-0.77 because ~40 shared boilerplate tokens outweigh one name token -- no IDF tweak lowers that below ask_threshold without regressing the D-no-duplicates eval bar (title-boost keeps them ~0.72; verified by simulation). The residual refusal is the DESIGNED 'ask' behaviour (R-dedupe-matchers: no score can tell a different instance of the same template from a duplicate; --new is the documented answer), and the semantic remedy is tracked as B-semantic-recall. (2) The 'printed the answer command four times identically' symptom is already fixed in 0.2.10: Bf29855c414 (commit 3a140e1c9) replaced repeated ready-commands with one 'Answer it:' line in ddflow/api/_dedupe_reason.py.

Fixes bug B-session-prompt-no-relay-attribution: Operator answers reach a subagent through the coordinator; ddflow session prompt has no field for relayed-by, so the log cannot distinguish the operator's own words from a relay. Found on DRV-decide.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-session-prompt-no-relay-attribution --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-session-prompt-no-relay-attribution --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B-session-prompt-no-relay-attribution: session prompt cannot mark a prompt as relayed by a coordinator

data.claim: The session.prompt path drops relay provenance: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py::prompt writes only text/item/redactions, so a relay is indistinguishable from the operator's own words. Adding relayed_by to that event and folding it makes the distinction recordable.
data.falsifier: A relayed prompt's event data shows no non-empty relayed_by distinct from a direct prompt's.
data.mechanism: prompt() accepts relayed_by, appends it to the session.prompt event data; _h_session_prompt folds it; api.session_prompt and both surfaces pass it; the CLI flag --relayed-by sets it, empty means direct.
data.probe: ddflow session prompt <sid> --text x --relayed-by coord-1 ; read the session.prompt event data
data.question: Can a ddflow session prompt record that it was relayed by a coordinator, so the log tells a relay from the operator's own words?

evidence.note: RESEARCH R3f07337b0b CONFIRMED: added relayed_by to session.prompt event + fold + both surfaces; probe shows relayed->relayed_by:'coord-1' vs direct->relayed_by:''

ddflow brief --item showed the rules digest; change is a small, config-free wiring of one field through appends/fold/surfaces; obeys r-everything-configurable (no new hard-coded tunable) and r-small-files. Commit 7892cb5be.

Added relayed_by through ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py::prompt (event data), ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py::_h_session_prompt (fold), ddflow/api/knowledge/sessions.py::session_prompt, surfaces/declared/records.py (--relayed-by Param) and surfaces/commands/knowledge.py (cmd_session). Regression test tests/test_session_prompt_relayed_by.py. Commit 7892cb5be.

chunk_findings.detail: When `relayed_by` is supplied but the same redacted text was recently captured by the prompt hook, `prompt` returns early from `_recorded_recently(log, clean, auto_only=True)` and never appends the `session.prompt` event. Example: an auto hook event already contains text `"approve"`; calling `session_prompt(repo, sid, "approve", relayed_by="coordinator")` returns without writing a new event, so `core/handlers/sessions.py` never sees `relayed_by` and the log still cannot distinguish the relay from the operator's direct words. The dedupe must be bypassed, or the existing event updated, when relay attribution is provided.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The new test bypasses the project's CLI/adapter harness by calling `subprocess.run` directly and constructing its own environment (`env = {**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT)}`). [r-adapters] requires external dependencies such as subprocess and environment access to go through ports/fakes, and explicitly says tests should use a fake instead of subprocess. This is not merely stylistic: if the test environment has required entries in `PYTHONPATH`, this line replaces them with only `ROOT`, so the subprocess `sys.executable -m ddflow ...` can fail to import a dependency; it also bypasses any isolation or environment setup performed by the imported `run_cli` helper.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_prompt_relayed_by.py:_cli

chunk_findings.detail: When `relayed_by` is non-empty, the new attribution can still be discarded by the existing dedup path. The check `if _recorded_recently(log, clean, auto_only=True): return n` is made before `log.append(... {..., "relayed_by": relayed_by, ...})`, and `_recorded_recently` is given only `clean`; it cannot see `relayed_by`. Concrete failure: a prompt hook auto-captures the text `"yes"` with `relayed_by=""`, and moments later the coordinator records the same relayed words via `A.session_prompt(repo, session, "yes", relayed_by="coordinator")`. The second call hits `_recorded_recently(...) == True`, returns before appending, and the session log keeps only the unrelayed `"yes"`, so bug B-session-prompt-no-relay-attribution remains for repeated short answers.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_cli` helper calls `subprocess.run` directly to invoke `python -m ddflow`, even though `run_cli` is already imported and used in the same file. Rule [r-adapters] requires subprocess tools to go through a port in `ddflow/adapters` and tests to use a fake rather than the real subprocess. The direct call bypasses that port, so a swap or isolated fake used by other tests will not cover this regression test path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_prompt_relayed_by.py:_cli

chunk_findings.detail: When `relayed_by` is non-empty, the duplicate-suppression check is skipped (`if not relayed_by and _recorded_recently(...)`). If the prompt hook has already captured the same operator text, the old code would return without appending; the new code appends a second `session.prompt` event. For example, after the hook records `text="approve"` as a recent auto prompt, `S.prompt(log, cfg, sid, "approve", relayed_by="coordinator")` creates two prompt events. `ddflow/core/handlers/sessions.py` then exposes two prompt entries, one with `relayed_by=""` and one with `relayed_by="coordinator"`, with different `seq` values. This makes replay/session view show two operator prompts, including a false unattributed direct prompt, reintroducing the ambiguity the change is meant to fix and contradicting the function’s own “not written again when the prompt hook already captured the same words” contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The change bypasses the existing duplicate suppression whenever `relayed_by` is non-empty (`if not relayed_by and _recorded_recently(...)`). In the intended relayed case, the prompt hook has already auto-captured the operator’s words a moment ago without attribution; `_recorded_recently` would otherwise return True. With this change, the same utterance is appended a second time as a separate `session.prompt` event: the earlier auto event still has `relayed_by=""` and the new event has `relayed_by="coordinator"`. A single relayed answer now appears as both “direct” and “relayed” in the log, duplicating it and still leaving the ambiguous direct entry the bug is meant to remove. The relay attribution should be recorded on the hook event itself, or the old hook event should be updated/suppressed, not cause an additional prompt event.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions/_record.py:prompt
